transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-02 15:30 UTC; Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Redwood Solutions), Lena Ortiz (CatalystGrid Head of Cloud Partnerships), Samir Q (Platform Eng), Ivy Ng (Security), Tom Russell (PM)

Auto-generated summary: quick checkin after initial PR to marketplace repo. need to validate onprem connector and VPC patterns.

--- Topics ---
- Packaging and listing format
- Connectivity patterns (VPC peering, NAT, reverse tunnel)
- KMS/HSM compatibility and audit logs
- Quantization and runtime variants for edge nodes
- Billing and metering expectations

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick rollcall, and then we'll jump into the hybrid listing flow.
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: Hi all, Lena here. Thanks, Maya.
[00:15] Samir Q: Samir on the call.
[00:18] Ivy Ng: Ivy here. security.
[00:20] Tom Russell: Tom, product.
[00:25] Devon Park: Devon from Redwood SE. I'll take most of the technical bits.
[00:28] Ravi Patel: Ravi, solutions. I'll coordinate the lab.

[00:35] Maya: Cool. Quick recap: we sent an initial marketplace package last week — the helm chart + runtime adapter — and the goal today is to confirm the network patterns for CatalystGrid so the listing doc and the refarch are accurate. Samir, can you walk through what you provisioned?
[00:51] Samir Q: Sure, so we stood up a staging VPC in eu-west-2, two subnets public/private, we tried to install the helm chart but hit an issue with the init container failing on the node affinity. I think that's on the chart side, not infra, but wanted to surface it.
[01:10] Devon: ok that sounds like the nodeSelector may be defaulting to gpu:true — we ship that optional — did you try the cpu-only override?
[01:18] Samir Q: we tried "gpu=false" but got a crashloop because the runtime was expecting a kv cache on startup. the docs mention kv cache but not that it's required for cold-start?
[01:30] Ravi: yeah, good catch — our chart has an optional redis kv cache but the >=v2 runtime autoconfig assumes a prefix cache unless you set REDWOOD_PREFIX_CACHE=false. sounds like we need to make that clearer.
[01:42] Maya: Action item there, we'll update the README and chart values. Devon, you ok to add that?
[01:47] Devon: absolutely. I'll change the default and add a note about cold start behavior.

[02:05] Ivy Ng: quick security note — from a compliance perspective, we need audit logs for key access and proof of KMS rotations. does Redwood's private offering integrate with external KMS or only Redwood-managed?
[02:20] Maya: Good question. For Redwood Private we support customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS / GCP KMS and we have a documented integration for HSM-backed keys in the on-prem package. You will get audit logs in the console and exportable syslog / S3 buckets.
[02:36] Tom: can you map how the key usage shows up in logs? e.g., which service principal?
[02:41] Devon: The runtime calls the KMS through the customer credentials we mount in the connector. The audit entries show the connector principal — it's in the draft mapping doc we shared (see link in chat). note that service principal names can look like redwood-runtime-<cluster>.
[02:55] Ivy: that mapping doc had some acronyms and a couple of typos, we couldn't match it to our audit schema. We'll send sample schemas.
[03:03] Lena: on the marketplace listing side we need clear docs for what runtime variants are supported and recommended defaults. our marketplace catalog enforces an umbrella metadata YAML — size limits, container scan results, and a connectivity guide. We need those artifacts to pass automatic validation.
[03:22] Maya: Understood. We can produce a compatibility matrix: runtime variant (hosted/dedicated/private), expected memory, vCPU, quantization level, and recommended image sizes. Dev, can you point to where quantization options are surfaced?
[03:35] Devon: yes. We have profiles: fp16 (full fp16), int8-q4, int4-q2 etc. The tradeoff is latency vs quality — we can provide sample P50/P95 for typical prompt lengths. For edge nodes where memory is tight, we recommend int8 with cached kv for prefix reuse.
[03:52] Samir Q: will the quantized builds be part of the marketplace package or pulled on-demand?
[03:58] Ravi: currently our packaging references model artifacts stored in Redwood's model storage; the chart downloads them on install. We can also make a variant that bundles a small quantized model for air-gapped installs — that's larger chart size but simpler install.
[04:13] Tom: For billing and metering, CatalystGrid expects per-token + per-request metrics to correlate customer spend. how does Redwood report usage when the runtime is running in our VPC vs Redwood-hosted?
[04:26] Maya: In Private mode we send anonymized telemetry to the control plane unless you choose full air-gap. When VPC-peered we can expose a metering probe that pushes usage counters to your billing endpoint via a secure TLS connection. We also support periodically shipping aggregated logs to S3 for reconciliations.
[04:44] Ivy: We need to ensure PII isn't sent — only counters. is there a HIPAA/PII safe-mode?
[04:52] Devon: yes, telemetry is token counts, latency buckets, and error codes only. payload masking is configurable; payloads are never sent by default. We'll include a telemetry configuration page in the docs.

[05:10] Lena: network topology question — our marketplace requires either a private connector that initiates an outbound tunnel to the marketplace control plane, or a peering setup. For enterprise customers we prefer peering. Can Redwood support both?
[05:22] Maya: We support both. Outbound connector (reverse tunnel) is the simplest for non-prod; peering is recommended for low-latency production. There are differences in how keys are managed and how failover is handled.
[05:36] Samir Q: if we peer, do you require external IPs on nodes? we have strict NAT policies.
[05:43] Devon: No, peering is L3 — no public IPs are required. We establish routes between subnets. For some customers we additionally use a private NAT gateway for egress to pull images.

[06:00] [short silence - note: background office noise]
[06:08] Ivy: On the KMS front, we also use an HSM provider (Entrust). We need to validate signing flows for model artifacts and that key rotation won't invalidate existing tokens.
[06:20] Ravi: We already support external HSMs, but the artifact signing flow is a newer ask. We can sign container images (cosign) as part of the build pipeline and validate at install time using supplied public keys. We need to sketch a small flow for rotation events.
[06:36] Maya: Let's make that an action item — show how cosign verification fits into the install and what happens on key rotation.

[07:05] Tom: Another customer requirement — some of our enterprise buyers want explicit latency SLOs in the marketplace listing. can you publish P50/P95 numbers per region and per tier?
[07:18] Devon: yes, we have benchmark artifacts. we'll provide P50/P95 for the sample 200-token prompt across hosted and dedicated variants. For Private it's more variable but we can provide a reference for typical hardware.

[07:35] Lena: about the marketplace metadata YAML — do you have a sample that includes the fields we need (costing matrix, image digest, telemetry hooks)?
[07:42] Maya: yes, we'll share a sample manifest. I'll attach it to the follow-up.

[08:00] Samir Q: we tried to run a simple inference and saw tokenization differences vs our tokenizer; outputs were slightly off. is that expected?
[08:10] Devon: There can be tokenization mismatches if your pre/post processors alter whitespace or Unicode normalization. We can add a debugging endpoint to show tokenization and canonicalization.
[08:23] Samir Q: that would help. also want to run a small quality test to compare embeddings.

[08:35] Ravi: We'll prepare a bench runbook — small dataset, three models, compare embedding cosine sim and generation perplexity. Devon will own the bench.

[09:00] Ivy: compliance - do you publish SOC2 or ISO attestation for the control plane?
[09:06] Maya: Redwood has SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 for the control plane. For Private we provide a compliance pack and can do customer audits on-site or remote. We'll share the compliance kit link.

[09:20] Tom: Any blockers we've seen so far?
[09:24] Samir Q: the only immediate blocker was the init container/node affinity + kv cache default. Otherwise the packaging validation will fail until we supply the marketplace metadata fields in the format they expect.
[09:36] Maya: So next steps — we'll update the helm chart defaults and README, share checklist and sample manifest, and schedule the lab. Ravi to coordinate the lab windows.

[09:49] Devon: I'll also attach a small troubleshooting script to surface tokenization and kv cache status on startup.
[09:58] Lena: Great. On our side we'll provision the peering for a test cluster and share credentials for the metering probe.

[10:12] [brief crosstalk about calendars and times]

[10:30] Ivy: small question on image scanning — does Redwood require an SBOM? our marketplace scanner looks for SBOM and CVE status.
[10:40] Ravi: we can emit SBOMs as part of our build pipeline. we'll include that in the sample packaging.

[11:00] Tom: Anything else?
[11:04] Maya: One last note — for air-gapped customers we recommend an offline bundle. We'll outline size tradeoffs and a checklist to create the bundle.

[11:15] Lena: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[11:18] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up with artifacts and set the lab date.

--- End ---

Shared artifacts referenced: marketplace-manifest-sample.yaml (link: https://drive.example.com/cg/marketplace-manifest-sample), redwood-packaging-checklist (https://redwood.example.com/internal/packaging-checklist), bench-runbook-template (https://redwood.example.com/bench/runbooks/hybrid-compatibility).
